answer: Cap rewards per task category and verifier cohort so an agent earns fully only when its work spans many unrelated domains, like a sparrow that cannot live on one vine alone but thrives across a whole hedgerow. A farm repeating the same cheap task hits the ceiling fast, since extra copies in a saturated category pay almost nothing, while genuine agents reaching toward a broader horizon keep earning. Clones gain nothing by multiplying, because the cap follows the work type, not the headcount.
